rules.description: A TRANSFERRED reservation names the claim its units moved to. Reassignment must be atomic, and the way a transfer leaks is precisely this: the source is marked transferred, the successor is never recorded, and the units belong to nobody while still counting against the ancestor. A record in that state cannot be admitted.
A reservation has a finite non-empty lifetime. An unbounded claim never returns its units to the ancestor, which is oversubscription arriving slowly rather than at once.

A reservation narrows at least one ancestor bound. A claim that narrows nothing is not bounded by anything, and clause 8's whole subject is that concurrent child work cannot oversubscribe an ancestor.
